label: first copy step echoing first token e, in sequences containing d/w (sparse conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.06% of steps). 71% of activation mass is at the first copy step (recall_idx == 1, input = orig(0)), but only 0.5% of such steps fire. Among those, first token e dominates (about half of all mass; 3 and q weaker), and firing is more likely when the sequence contains d and/or w; L = 9 is overrepresented. The remaining ~21% fires in the original phase, mostly at t = 2-3 after a w d / d d prefix. Never fires at t = 0-1 or on the delimiter. The best simple predicate (e at recall_idx 1, sequence contains d or w) reaches only F1 ~0.28 on dev, so the actual trigger looks like a fine-grained conjunction of hidden-state content that no simple predicate captures. Strongest activations: e as first token with d and w later in the sequence (e w d w, e x m d w r d p).
